batchName: Empire: Claudius and Nero (AD 41-68) - Easy Batch 2

questions.question: Which group did Claudius rely on to run the offices for letters, finance and justice?
questions.explanation: Claudius put freedmen in charge of separate offices for letters, finance and justice. Senators were appalled, whispering that the freedmen ruled their master.
questions.sourceQuote: To run the empire day to day, he relied on freedmen (*liberti*), former slaves, who headed separate offices for letters, finance and justice.

questions.question: What was the first target of Boudica's revolt?
questions.explanation: The rebels first attacked Camulodunum, a colony of veterans hated for its expensive temple to Claudius. Survivors held out in that temple for two days.
questions.sourceQuote: Their first target was Camulodunum, modern Colchester, a colony of Roman veterans hated for its expensive temple to the god-emperor Claudius.

questions.question: What did a childhood illness leave Claudius with?
options: A limp, a stammer and a shaking head
Blindness in one eye and deafness
A withered arm and a hunched back
questions.explanation: Illness left Claudius with a limp, a stammer and a shaking head. Modern doctors have guessed at polio, cerebral palsy or Tourette syndrome.
questions.sourceQuote: He belonged to the very top of Rome's ruling family, but as a child he suffered an illness that left him with a limp, a stammer and a shaking head.

questions.question: In what year did Claudius send legions to invade Britain?
questions.explanation: In AD 43 Claudius sent four legions across the Channel after a British ally driven from his lands appealed for help.
questions.sourceQuote: In AD 43, after a British ally driven from his lands appealed for help, Claudius sent four legions (*legiones*), Rome's heavy infantry divisions of several thousand men each, across the Channel.

questions.question: Where was Claudius born, making him the first Roman emperor born outside Italy?
questions.explanation: Claudius was born at Lugdunum, modern Lyon, in 10 BC. Fittingly, a speech of his admitting Gallic nobles to the Senate was later found on a bronze plaque at Lyon.
questions.sourceQuote: Claudius was born in 10 BC at Lugdunum, modern Lyon in France, the first Roman emperor born outside Italy.

questions.question: Whom did Nero have killed in AD 59, according to ancient writers after a staged shipwreck?
questions.explanation: A freedman arranged a shipwreck; when Agrippina swam ashore, he murdered her and called it suicide. Historians agree Nero's conduct grew far worse afterwards.
questions.sourceQuote: In AD 59 Nero had his mother killed: according to ancient writers, a freedman arranged a shipwreck, and when she swam ashore he murdered her and called it suicide.

questions.question: What happened when Nero competed at the Olympic Games in AD 67?
options: He won every contest, even an unfinished race
He refused to compete against Greek rivals
He was badly injured and fled back to Rome
He lost every event and left in disgrace
questions.explanation: Nero won every contest, including a chariot race in which he fell out and never finished. Romans associated such performing with slaves and entertainers.
questions.sourceQuote: In AD 67 he competed at the Olympic Games in Greece and won every contest, including a chariot race in which he fell out and never finished.

questions.question: Almost everything we know about Claudius and Nero comes from how many ancient writers?
questions.explanation: The three are Tacitus, a biographer of the emperors and a later Greek senator. All came from Rome's upper classes and usually took the Senate's side.
questions.sourceQuote: Almost everything we know about Claudius and Nero comes from three writers: Tacitus, the senator-historian, a biographer of the emperors and a later Greek senator.

questions.question: Which of Claudius's building projects failed spectacularly, flooding a gladiator show?
options: A tunnel to drain the Fucine Lake
questions.explanation: The drainage tunnel for the Fucine Lake was too small, and its flood swamped a gladiator show, sending Claudius running for his life. His two new aqueducts of AD 52, by contrast, succeeded.
questions.sourceQuote: One project failed spectacularly: a tunnel to drain the Fucine Lake in central Italy was too small, and when opened its flood swamped a gladiator show, sending the emperor running for his life.

questions.question: According to tradition, where was Claudius found hiding after his nephew's murder?
options: Inside a temple on the Capitol
In a boat on the Tiber
Behind a curtain in the palace
In a cellar under the Senate house
questions.explanation: Tradition says a guardsman found him cowering behind a curtain and hailed him emperor instead of killing him. He was then hurried off to the guards' camp.
questions.sourceQuote: According to tradition, a guardsman found him cowering behind a curtain and, instead of killing him, hailed him as emperor.
